newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish July external reserves down 177 mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Irish July external reserves down 177 mln punts.

text.p: Ireland's official external reserves fell by 177 million Irish pounds to 4.871 billion in July, the Central Bank of Ireland said on Thursday.
"Interest and principal payments on the Exchequer foreign debt exceeded EU transfers and net positive foreign-exchange market intervention," the central bank said in a statement.
The money market shortage fell by 79 million punts in July, mainly due to government and NTMA transactions.
Net redemption of government securities exceeded net government tax receipts and the impact of transactions by the National Treasury Management Agency with commercial banks, the central bank said.
The central bank said it supplied support to the money market of 951 million at end-July compared with 1.03 billion at end-June.
Support through sale and repurchase agreements fell by 81 million while borrowing through the short-term facility rate fell by four million to 11.0 million punts.
